basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A unit is a part of an organization created by that organization, with no legal personality of its own.
It is distinct from a position (WM-ORG-004) placed in it and from the people assigned to those positions.
It differs from a site or location; one unit can span several sites and one site can host several units.
Structure changes are reorganization acts with decision records, not attribute edits.

may: Reconstruct the unit structure as of a given date.
Derive an org chart projection from authoritative structure data.
Reconcile unit data with a directory and report differences.
Compute headcount rollups above the declared minimum cell size.
mustNot: Create, rename or reparent a unit without a decision of the parent organization.
Let a directory or downstream system overwrite the authoritative structure.
Publish staffing figures below the minimum cell size.
Delete a disbanded unit together with its lineage links.
requiresHuman: Assigning or changing a unit's mandate and delegated authority.
Resolving a conflict between overlapping unit mandates.

considerations: Small units can make individual staff identifiable in reported figures; suppression protects them.
Reorganizations affect jobs and working conditions; changes should be traceable and lawful.
Accountability should match authority, so no unit is blamed for matters it does not control.

items: A unit has a name, a parent organization, a parent unit and a mandate, and appears in org charts and directories.
Confused with a team (WM-ORG-003), a cost centre, a site and a legal subsidiary.
Wrong reporting lines route approvals to the wrong manager.
Stale directory structure grants or keeps access that should have ended.
Lost lineage makes historical decisions and records impossible to attribute.
